heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Global Hiring without a local entity
heroData.description: Expand your team into Cyprus quickly and securely using an Employer of Record. We handle local payroll, benefits, and strict compliance with Cypriot labor laws, allowing you to focus on growth.
heroData.bestFor: International companies hiring Cyprus-based remote talent or local staff without a branch office.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Compliance Review
steps.description: Drafting of a Cyprus-compliant employment contract in Greek and English. Ensuring compliance with the Protection of Wages Law and the Organization of Working Time Law. Probation periods are typically 6 months but can be extended up to 2 years by mutual agreement.

steps.title: Employee Documentation Collection
steps.description: Collection of mandatory documents: Passport/ID copy, Social Insurance Number (if available), Tax ID Number (TIC), and proof of address. For non-EU nationals, additional work permit/visa documentation is required.

steps.title: Social Insurance & Tax Registration
steps.description: Registration of the employee with the Cyprus Social Insurance Services and the Tax Department. This must be completed before or within the first month of employment to avoid penalties.

steps.title: Benefits & Health System (GeSY) Setup
steps.description: Enrollment in the General Healthcare System (GeSY). Optional setup for supplementary private medical insurance or provident funds, which are common 'perks' for professional roles in Cyprus.

steps.title: First Payroll Run & Ongoing Management
steps.description: Finalizing the first month's payroll. The EOR handles monthly salary disbursements, tax withholdings (PAYE), and social contribution payments on behalf of the client.

rows.label: Social Cohesion Fund
values: Calculated on total earnings without cap

rows.label: Total Employer Burden
values: Excluding optional holiday fund and 13th month bonus

items.title: Termination and Notice Periods
items.text: Notice periods in Cyprus are strictly statutory based on length of service: 1 week (after 26 weeks) up to 8 weeks (after 312+ weeks). Termination during probation is easier but must be documented clearly to avoid 'unfair dismissal' claims.

items.title: 13th Month Salary Custom
items.text: While not legally mandatory unless specified in a collective agreement, the '13th month' salary is a widespread cultural expectation in Cyprus, typically paid in December. Most competitive EOR contracts include this provision.

items.title: Non-EU National Hiring
items.text: Hiring non-EU nationals through an EOR in Cyprus is possible but involves complex 'BC' (Business Center) company requirements. Ensure your EOR partner has the specific license to sponsor third-country nationals.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: Having senior employees (decision-makers) on local EOR payroll for extended periods can trigger PE risks for the parent company. Consult with tax experts if hiring management-level staff.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through a PEO in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, many EOR providers offer 'Contractor of Record' services. This is ideal for short-term projects but carries misclassification risk if the contractor works like a full-time employee (e.g., fixed hours, company equipment).

faqs.question: What is the minimum wage in Cyprus for 2025?
faqs.answer: The national minimum wage in Cyprus is €1,000 per month (after 6 months of service with the same employer), and €940 upon recruitment. Some sectors may have higher minimums via collective agreements.

faqs.question: How are public holidays handled?
faqs.answer: Cyprus has 15-16 public holidays annually. If an employee works on a public holiday, they are typically entitled to a premium rate (usually 1:2) or a compensatory day off, depending on the contract.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory for EOR employees?
faqs.answer: The General Healthcare System (GeSY) is mandatory and covered by social contributions. However, most professional EOR packages include supplemental private health and life insurance to attract top tier talent.

steps.title: Data Gathering & Variable Input
steps.description: Collection of monthly variable data including overtime hours, commissions, bonuses, and any unpaid leave or sick days. Input for 13th-month accruals if applicable.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculations
steps.description: Calculation of gross salary, deduction of Social Insurance (8.8%), GeSY (2.65%), and PAYE income tax based on the employee's specific tax code. Employer contributions are also calculated simultaneously.

steps.title: Approval & Funding
steps.description: Review and approval of the payroll register by the client. Funding of the total payroll amount (Net + Taxes + Contributions) to the payroll provider's client trust account.

steps.title: Disbursement & Filing
steps.description: Direct deposit of net salaries to employee bank accounts (typically via SEPA). Electronic filing of IR7 (Employer's Return) and payment of social insurance to the Social Insurance Services via Sisnet.

steps.title: Reporting & Payslips
steps.description: Delivery of digital, compliant payslips to employees. Generation of monthly accounting journals (ERP integration) and year-end T.D.63 certificates for employees.

items.title: Social Insurance Deadlines
items.text: Payments of social insurance contributions and GeSY must be made by the end of the month following the month of employment. Late payments incur an 11% penalty (prorated).

items.title: Special 50% Tax Exemption
items.text: Expats earning over €55,000 per year may qualify for a 50% income tax exemption for 17 years. This requires strict documentation of 'non-resident status' prior to employment.

items.title: Payslip Requirements
items.text: Under the Protection of Wages Law, employers must provide a written or electronic payslip for every payment. It must clearly state gross pay, all deductions, and the net amount.

items.title: Digital Signatures for Contracts
items.text: Cyprus fully recognizes electronic signatures (eIDAS compliant). Using platforms like DocuSign for employment contracts is standard practice for modern payroll setups.

sections.title: How to Use the Payroll Calculator
sections.subtitle: Accurate Results in 3 Steps

steps.title: Enter Gross Monthly/Annual Salary
steps.description: Input the base salary. Specify if you receive a 13th-month bonus, as this will spread the tax calculations over 13 periods.

steps.title: Select Residency & Tax Status
steps.description: Choose between 'Resident' and 'Non-Resident'. Apply the 50% tax exemption if you are a first-time expat earning over €55,000 annually.

steps.title: Review Detailed Breakdown
steps.description: The calculator instantly generates your Net Pay, PAYE withholding, Social Insurance (8.8%), and GeSY (2.65%) deductions.

items.title: 50% Tax Exemption for Expats
items.text: Individuals who were not residents for the last 10 years and earn >€55k/year are entitled to a 50% tax exemption for 17 years. This is a major draw for senior international talent.

items.title: Social Insurance Ceiling
items.text: Social Insurance contributions are capped at an annual gross salary of €66,612 (for 2025). Any income above this amount is only subject to GeSY and PAYE.

items.title: Provident Fund Contributions
items.text: While optional, many Cyprus companies offer Provident Funds. Employee contributions (usually 5%) are tax-deductible up to a combined limit of 1/6th of taxable income.

faqs.question: Does the calculator include the 13th salary?
faqs.answer: Yes, our calculator allows you to toggle the 13th salary option, which is standard in Cyprus and affects the monthly net distribution.

faqs.question: What is GeSY and do I have to pay it?
faqs.answer: GeSY is the National Healthcare System. It is mandatory for all employees (2.65% deduction) regardless of whether they have private health insurance.

faqs.question: Is the tax-free bracket applied monthly?
faqs.answer: Technically, the €19,500 exemption is annual, but employers apply it pro-rata on a monthly basis to equalize your take-home pay throughout the year.

faqs.question: Can I calculate for self-employed status?
faqs.answer: Yes, our calculator has a toggle for self-employed professionals. Note that social insurance rates for self-employed individuals (currently ~16.6%) differ from standard employees.

heroData.title: Incorporation and Entity Setup in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Establish your business in a premier EU financial hub
heroData.description: Cyprus offers one of the most attractive tax regimes in the EU, combined with a robust legal framework based on English Common Law. We provide end-to-end support for company formation, from name reservation to bank account opening.
heroData.bestFor: Startups, holding companies, and international businesses seeking a strategic gateway to Europe and the Middle East.

steps.title: Name Approval & Reservation
steps.description: Submission of at least three proposed names to the Registrar of Companies for approval. Approval typically takes 3-5 business days for standard applications. The name must be unique and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. We recommend checking for trademark conflicts before submission.

steps.title: Drafting Constitutional Documents
steps.description: Preparation of the Memorandum and Articles of Association by a qualified Cyprus lawyer. This includes defining the company's objects, share capital structure, and governance rules. These documents must be in Greek, though English translations are typically provided for international clients.

steps.title: KYC & Compliance Submission
steps.description: Subscription of shares by the initial shareholders and notarization of the He1 (statutory declaration), He2 (registered office), and He3 (directors/secretary) forms. Submission of the full application package including passport copies and proof of address for all officers to the Registrar.

steps.title: Issuance of Corporate Certificates
steps.description: Upon formal approval, the Registrar issues a set of certified certificates: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Directors and Secretary, Certificate of Shareholders, and Certificate of Registered Office. These are the primary documents required for opening bank accounts.

steps.title: Post-Incorporation Registrations
steps.description: Mandatory registration with the Tax Department for a Tax Identification Code (TIC). VAT registration is required if the annual taxable turnover exceeds €15,600. Additionally, the company must register as an employer with the Social Insurance Services.

items.title: Tax Residence Importance
items.text: To benefit from the 12.5% corporate tax rate, the company must be managed and controlled from Cyprus. This usually requires having a majority of local directors and substantial economic presence (substance) on the island.

items.title: Intellectual Property (IP) Box
items.text: Cyprus offers a highly competitive IP Box regime where 80% of qualifying profits from IP assets are exempt from tax, resulting in an effective tax rate as low as 2.5%.

items.title: Banking Challenges
items.text: Opening a corporate bank account in Cyprus is a rigorous process due to strict AML/KYC regulations. Expect a timeline of 4-8 weeks and prepare extensive documentation on business activities and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs).

faqs.question: What is the minimum share capital for a Cyprus company?
faqs.answer: There is no legal minimum share capital for a private limited company. However, it is standard practice to incorporate with an authorized share capital of €1,000, usually divided into 1,000 shares of €1 each.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a Cyprus company?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are no restrictions on the nationality or residency of shareholders. A single individual or corporate entity can hold all the shares.

faqs.question: Is a local secretary required?
faqs.answer: Yes, every Cyprus company must appoint a secretary. While they don't have to be a resident, it is highly recommended to appoint a local professional to ensure all statutory filings with the Registrar are handled correctly.

heroData.title: Staffing and Talent Acquisition in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Tap into a highly skilled, multilingual talent pool
heroData.description: Cyprus is home to a growing hub of tech, finance, and maritime talent. Our recruitment experts help you navigate the local market to find the best candidates, from senior executive searches to high-volume staffing solutions.
heroData.bestFor: Companies looking to build local teams in Nicosia, Limassol, or Larnaca, particularly in FinTech, iGaming, and Professional Services.

steps.title: Market Benchmarking
steps.description: Analysis of current salary trends in Cyprus for the specific role. Professional roles in Limassol (the tech hub) often command 15-20% higher salaries than other regions.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Sourcing
steps.description: Tapping into local job boards (like Ergodotisi), LinkedIn, and specialized talent pools. For niche roles, headhunting from the established iGaming and Forex sectors is common.

steps.title: Screening & Cultural Assessment
steps.description: Technical screening followed by an assessment of cultural fit. Multilingual capabilities (English, Greek, Russian, Arabic) are frequently a high priority for international firms based in Cyprus.

steps.title: Interview Management
steps.description: Coordinating multiple rounds of interviews. In the post-2023 market, candidates expect a streamlined process with no more than 3 stages to avoid 'ghosting' or losing talent to competitors.

steps.title: Offer Negotiation & Background Checks
steps.description: Managing the offer process, including 13th-month salary discussions and benefits packages. Background checks in Cyprus typically involve verifying previous employment and educational credentials.

items.title: Remote vs. Hybrid Trends
items.text: While Cyprus is a small island, talent in the tech sector increasingly demands hybrid work (2-3 days in office). Fully remote roles from Cyprus-based companies are rare but becoming more common to attract international talent.

items.title: Talent Scarcity in STEM
items.text: There is a significant shortage of senior developers and data scientists in Cyprus. Competition is fierce among the 100+ FinTech and iGaming companies relocating to the island.

items.title: Leveraging 'Headquartering' Incentives
items.text: Cyprus recently introduced new visa categories (Fast-Track Business Activation) which make it easier for international companies to bring in specialists from abroad if they cannot find local talent.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period for candidates in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: For professional roles, the standard notice period is usually 1 month. Senior executives or specialized technical talent may have notice periods of 2-3 months.

faqs.question: Do I need to advertise job roles in Greek?
faqs.answer: No, for international businesses, advertising in English is standard. Most professional candidates in Cyprus are highly fluent in English, which is the primary language of business for international sectors.

faqs.question: Are background checks mandatory in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: They are not legally mandatory for all roles but are standard practice in the financial services (CySEC regulated) and gaming sectors. Criminal record certificates from the Cyprus Police may be required for certain roles.

items.title: The importance of 'The 13th Month'
items.text: In Cyprus, the 13th-month salary is not just a bonus; it is often viewed as a fundamental part of the compensation package. Candidates expect to discuss this early in the negotiation phase.

items.title: Work-Life Balance Expectations
items.text: Cypriot work culture values productivity during office hours followed by strong boundaries for personal time. Companies that respect the 'right to disconnect' report 40% higher employee retention rates.

items.title: Multilingual Requirements
items.text: For roles involving local administration or customer service, Greek fluency is essential. However, the tech sector is almost exclusively English-speaking, often with a high demand for Russian or Hebrew speakers depending on the firm's origin.

items.title: Employee Benefits Trends
items.text: Beyond salary, private health insurance (to supplement GeSY) and flexible working hours are the most requested perks in the 2025 talent market.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Streamline your workforce management with modern HR Tech
heroData.description: Navigate the complexity of Cyprus labor laws with integrated HRIS platforms. Our recommended solutions combine employee self-service, automated leave management, and localized payroll capabilities tailored for the Cyprus market.
heroData.bestFor: SMEs and growing international firms seeking to digitize their HR operations and maintain compliance with local reporting requirements.

steps.title: Requirement Mapping & Tool Selection
steps.description: Identifying key needs such as GeSY contribution tracking, automated 13th-month calculations, and localized social insurance reporting. Selecting a platform that supports double-entry for multi-entity setups.

steps.title: Data Migration & Validation
steps.description: Importing existing employee records, historical payroll data, and leave balances. Ensuring all data is cleaned and mapped to the new system's structure according to GDPR standards.

steps.title: Localization & Rule Configuration
steps.description: Configuring Cyprus-specific labor rules, including the 38-40 hour work week, mandatory rest periods, and local public holiday calendars for 2025/2026.

steps.title: Employee & Manager Training
steps.description: Deploying self-service portals for leave requests, payslip access, and expense management. Training managers on approval workflows and performance tracking modules.

steps.title: Go-Live & Parallel Payroll Run
steps.description: Running the first live payroll through the HRIS while maintaining a parallel check against legacy systems to ensure 100% accuracy in tax and social contribution withholdings.

items.title: Digital Transformation in HR
items.text: Post-Pandemic, 70% of Cyprus-based international firms have transitioned to cloud-based HRIS. Local providers are increasingly integrating with the government's Sisnet portal for automated social insurance filings.

items.title: GDPR and Data Residency
items.text: As an EU member, Cyprus enforces strict GDPR compliance. Ensure your HRIS provider stores employee data on EU-based servers and provides robust data processing agreements (DPAs).

items.title: Mobile-First Accessibility
items.text: The Cyprus workforce is highly mobile. Apps that offer mobile-friendly 'Self-Service' portals for leave applications and pulse surveys see much higher engagement rates among younger talent.

faqs.question: Does HRIS software handle Cyprus leave laws automatically?
faqs.answer: Modern platforms can be configured to track the 20/24 days of annual leave (based on a 5/6 day work week) and the 15-day sick leave provision commonly found in Cyprus collective agreements.

faqs.question: Are there local HRIS providers in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, several local firms offer bespoke solutions that are deeply integrated with the Cyprus Tax Department and Social Insurance system, which can be advantageous for complex local entities.

faqs.question: Can I integrate HRIS with my Cyprus bookkeeping software?
faqs.answer: Most cloud HRIS platforms offer API integrations or CSV exports compatible with popular accounting tools used in Cyprus, such as QuickBooks, Xero, or Sage.

heroData.title: Accounting and Audit Services in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Professional financial oversight in an international business center
heroData.description: Maintain impeccable financial records with our comprehensive accounting and audit services. We ensure your business stays compliant with IFRS standards and the Cyprus Companies Law, providing transparency for stakeholders and tax authorities.
heroData.bestFor: Cyprus-registered companies requiring statutory annual audits, VAT compliance, and day-to-day bookkeeping.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping & Reconciliation
steps.description: Processing of sales/purchase invoices and bank reconciliation. Maintaining the general ledger according to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

steps.title: Quarterly VAT & VIES Returns
steps.description: Preparation and submission of quarterly VAT returns. Filing of VIES (VAT Information Exchange System) forms for intra-EU trade of goods and services.

steps.title: Annual Audit Preparation
steps.description: Collection of all supporting documentation for the mandatory annual statutory audit. This must be conducted by a registered auditor in Cyprus.

steps.title: Financial Statement Issuance
steps.description: Finalizing the audited financial statements. Presentation to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting (AGM) for approval.

steps.title: Regulatory Filings
steps.description: Filing of the HE32 (Annual Return) with the Registrar of Companies along with the audited financial statements. Deadline is usually 28 days after the AGM.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Cyprus was one of the first countries to fully adopt IFRS. All registered companies, regardless of size, must prepare financial statements in accordance with IFRS as adopted by the EU.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Failure to file the HE32 annual return on time results in an immediate €50 penalty, plus €1 per day for the first 6 months, and €2 per day thereafter, capped at €500 per return.

items.title: Benefit of Small Company Audit Exemption
items.text: While most companies require an audit, very small companies (meeting specific criteria: Turnover <€70k, Assets <€1M) may qualify for simplified reporting, though professional advice is highly recommended.

faqs.question: What is the financial year-end in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: The standard financial year-end is December 31st. However, companies can apply to have a different year-end to align with their parent company.

faqs.question: Are accounting records required to be kept in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, every company must keep proper books of account at its registered office in Cyprus or at such other place as the directors think fit.

faqs.question: How long must accounting records be kept?
faqs.answer: Under Cyprus tax law, accounting records and supporting documentation must be retained for at least six years from the end of the relevant tax year.

steps.title: Year-End Closing
steps.description: Finalizing the trial balance, reconciling all bank accounts, and ensuring all accruals and prepayments are correctly recorded as of December 31st.

steps.title: Preparation of Financial Statements
steps.description: Drafting of the full set of financial statements in accordance with IFRS, including the statement of financial position, profit or loss, and required disclosures.

steps.title: Audit Fieldwork & Substantiation
steps.description: Independent auditors review the records, perform sampling, and verify the existence and valuation of assets and liabilities. This often includes bank and debtor confirmations.

steps.title: Tax Computation & Review
steps.description: Calculating the final corporate tax liability after adjusting for tax-exempt income (e.g., dividend income) and non-deductible expenses.

steps.title: Signing & Statutory Submission
steps.description: Approval of the statements by the Board, signing by the auditors, and filing the HE32 annual return with the Registrar of Companies.

steps.title: UBO Register Maintenance
steps.description: Mandatory identification and reporting of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) to the central Registrar of Companies. Changes must be reported within 14 days.

steps.title: AML/KYC Framework Setup
steps.description: Implementation of Anti-Money Laundering procedures. This includes client due diligence, transaction monitoring, and regular staff training in accordance with ICPAC or CySEC guidelines.

steps.title: GDPR Documentation & Privacy
steps.description: Appointing a Data Protection Officer (if required) and maintaining a Record of Processing Activities (ROPA). Ensuring privacy policies and cookies are fully compliant with EU law.

steps.title: Annual General Meeting (AGM)
steps.description: Coordinating and documenting the mandatory Annual General Meeting. Preparing minutes to approve financial statements and re-elect directors/auditors.

steps.title: Economic Substance Reporting
steps.description: Ensuring the company meets the required level of presence in Cyprus. This involves verifying that core income-generating activities are performed locally.

items.title: Strike-Off Risk
items.text: The Registrar of Companies has become increasingly aggressive in striking off companies that fail to file their annual returns or UBO data. A strike-off can lead to the asset freezing of the company.

items.title: Regulated Sector Oversight
items.text: Companies in the Financial Services (CySEC) and Betting/iGaming (NBA) sectors face significantly higher compliance burdens, including monthly reporting and stricter minimum capital requirements.

items.title: Internal Compliance Audits
items.text: Conducting a voluntary annual compliance 'health check' can prevent major issues during bank account reviews or government audits. Focus on the validity of registrations and tax certificates.

faqs.question: Who is considered a UBO in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Any natural person who ultimately owns or controls more than 25% plus one share or ownership interest in the company, either directly or indirectly.

faqs.question: Does my company need a compliance officer?
faqs.answer: For standard holding or trading companies, a dedicated officer is not required (the secretary usually handles filings). However, for CySEC or ICPAC regulated firms, it is a mandatory role.

faqs.question: What happens if a company is struck off?
faqs.answer: The company ceases to exist as a legal entity, and all its assets (including bank accounts and property) are considered bona vacantia and vest in the Republic. Restoration is possible but involves a court application and significant legal fees.

steps.title: Provisional Tax Estimates
steps.description: Submission of provisional tax estimates for the current year. Payments are made in two equal installments: 31st July and 31st December. This avoids interest on underpayments.

steps.title: Annual Tax Return (TD4) Submission
steps.description: Preparation and electronic filing of the company's annual income tax return. The return is based on the audited financial statements and must be filed by March 31st of the year following the year-end.

steps.title: Capital Gains Tax Assessment
steps.description: Evaluation of any disposals of immovable property located in Cyprus or shares in companies owning such property. Tax rate is fixed at 20% on the gain.

steps.title: Special Defense Contribution (SDC)
steps.description: Calculation of SDC on 'unearned' income (dividends, interest, and rental income) for Cyprus-resident and domiciled companies. Note that non-domiciled individuals are exempt from SDC.

steps.title: Double Tax Treaty Application
steps.description: Leveraging Cyprus's extensive network of over 65 Double Tax Treaties to minimize withholding taxes on dividends, interest, and royalties paid from or to other jurisdictions.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax
values: Moving to 15% for global firms with >€750M revenue

rows.label: Value Added Tax (VAT)
values: Reduced rates of 0%, 5%, and 9% for certain goods

rows.label: Personal Income Tax
values: First €19,500 of annual income is tax-free

rows.label: SDC on Dividends
values: 0% for non-tax residents and non-domiciled individuals

rows.label: SDC on Interest
values: Reduced to 3% in certain corporate contexts

rows.label: Effective IP Tax Rate
values: Under the Nexus-compliant IP Box regime

items.title: Non-Domicile Status
items.text: Individuals who relocate to Cyprus and haven't been residents for 17 of the last 20 years qualify for 'Non-Dom' status. This provides an almost total exemption from tax on dividends and interest for 17 years.

items.title: DAC6 Reporting Requirements
items.text: Cyprus enforces strict mandatory disclosure rules (DAC6) for cross-border tax arrangements. Ensure all complex structures are reviewed by a tax lawyer to avoid heavy penalties for non-disclosure.

items.title: Group Relief Provision
items.text: Cyprus allows for 'Group Relief,' where current-year tax losses of one company can be set off against the profits of another company in the same group (75% ownership required).

faqs.question: Is there inheritance tax in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: No, inheritance and succession tax was abolished in Cyprus on January 1st, 2000. There is also no gift tax, although certain transfers must be reported.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for shipping companies?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cyprus has a world-class 'Tonnage Tax' system. Qualifying shipowners and charterers can opt to be taxed based on the net tonnage of their fleet rather than on corporation tax.

faqs.question: What is the 'Notional Interest Deduction' (NID)?
faqs.answer: NID is a tax deduction available to companies that introduce new equity into their business. It is calculated by multiplying the new equity by a reference interest rate, effectively reducing the corporate tax burden.

steps.title: 31 January
steps.description: Submission of the declaration of deemed dividend distribution (TD623) for profits earned two years prior.

steps.title: 31 March
steps.description: Deadline for the electronic submission of the previous year's Corporate Income Tax Return (TD4) and Personal Income Tax Return (TD1).

steps.title: 31 July
steps.description: Submission of the provisional tax return for the current year and payment of the 1st installment of provisional tax.

steps.title: 1 August
steps.description: Payment of the previous year's final corporation tax through the self-assessment system.

steps.title: 31 December
steps.description: Payment of the 2nd installment of provisional tax for the current year and final date for SDC and GeSY payments on dividends/interest.

heroData.title: Legal and Master Service Agreements in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Robust legal architecture for international business
heroData.description: Cyprus's legal system is based on English Common Law, providing a familiar and reliable framework for global businesses. We specialize in drafting comprehensive Master Service Agreements (MSAs), safeguarding intellectual property, and ensuring regulatory compliance for your Mediterranean operations.
heroData.bestFor: International service providers, software houses, and traders requiring high-quality legal documentation and risk management.

steps.title: Scope Definition & KPI Alignment
steps.description: Defining the precise scope of services, deliverables, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to avoid project creep and disputes.

steps.title: Liability & Indemnity Framework
steps.description: Drafting robust limitation of liability clauses and indemnification provisions tailored to Cyprus law and international standards.

steps.title: Intellectual Property (IP) Protection
steps.description: Ensuring clear ownership and transfer of IP rights. Specifically critical for software development or creative services delivered from Cyprus.

steps.title: Dispute Resolution & Governing Law
steps.description: Defining the governing law (standardly Cyprus or English law) and the mechanism for dispute resolution, such as LCIA arbitration or Cyprus court litigation.

steps.title: Termination & Exit Management
steps.description: Drafting 'exit' clauses that define notice periods, data transfer obligations, and final payment terms to ensure a smooth transition upon contract completion.

items.title: Common Law Heritage
items.text: Cyprus's legal framework is heavily influenced by English Common Law, making it highly compatible with UK and US business practices. Case law from English courts is often cited in Cyprus courts.

items.title: Stamp Duty Requirements
items.text: Contracts executed in Cyprus or relating to property/matters in Cyprus must be stamped. Failure to stamp within 30 days of execution leads to penalties and can make documents inadmissible in court.

items.title: Commercial Court Availability
items.text: Recent reforms have introduced specialized 'Commercial Courts' in Cyprus to handle large-value disputes (>€2M), aiming to drastically reduce the timeframe for legal resolutions.

faqs.question: Can I use English law for my Cyprus-based contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, freedom of contract allows parties to choose the governing law. English Law is very common in Cyprus-related transactions, especially in maritime, complex financing, and shareholder agreements, due to its predictability.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures legally binding in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cyprus follows the EU eIDAS regulation. Qualified Electronic Signatures (QES) have the same legal standing as handwritten signatures and are increasingly used for commercial lease agreements and service contracts.

faqs.question: How long does a dispute take in Cyprus courts?
faqs.answer: Standard litigation can take 3-5 years for a final judgment. However, the introduction of the new specialized Commercial court and the increasing popularity of mediation and arbitration are providing faster alternatives for business-to-business disputes.

steps.title: Execution by Directors
steps.description: Signing of the agreement by the authorized directors as per the company's articles. The corporate seal is often required for formal deeds.

steps.title: Certification by Certifying Officer
steps.description: For certain documents, signatures must be witnessed and certified by a local Certifying Officer (similar to a Notary Public) to confirm the identity of the signatories.

steps.title: Payment of Stamp Duty
steps.description: Calculation and payment of the applicable stamp duty based on the contract value. The stamps must be affixed to the document to ensure it can be used in a Cyprus court.

steps.title: Apostille (if for foreign use)
steps.description: If the agreement is to be used outside the EU, it should be sent to the Ministry of Justice for an Apostille under the Hague Convention.

heroData.title: Enterprise Software Solutions in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Accelerate Digital Innovation from the Mediterranean's Premier Tech Hub
heroData.description: Cyprus has rapidly emerged as a premier destination for software R&D, digital product development, and high-tech innovation. Our software solutions leverage the island's burgeoning talent pool and state-of-the-art digital infrastructure to deliver scalable, secure, and fully compliant software products for global enterprises. From FinTech platforms to complex SaaS architectures, we help you build the technology of tomorrow while benefiting from the island's unique strategic location and tax incentives for IP development.
heroData.bestFor: International tech companies, startups, and established firms seeking to establish R&D centers or outsource high-quality development within the European Union.

steps.title: Discovery & Architecture Design
steps.description: Workshop to define MVP requirements and system architecture. Selection of tech stacks (e.g., React, Node.js, Python) optimized for scalability and local hosting options.

steps.title: Sprint Planning & Rapid Prototyping
steps.description: Defining 2-week agile sprints. Creating high-fidelity wireframes and interactive prototypes to align stakeholder expectations early.

steps.title: Development & Continuous Integration
steps.description: Core coding phase with automated testing and CI/CD pipelines. Ensuring code adheres to high security standards (OWASP) and local data residency laws.

steps.title: QA & User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
steps.description: Rigorous testing across devices and environments. Conducting UAT with client teams to ensure all business logic and compliance rules are met.

steps.title: Deployment & Managed Support
steps.description: Coordinated launch on cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/Google Cloud). Ongoing maintenance, security patches, and iterative feature updates.

items.title: IP Box Tax Incentive
items.text: Cyprus offers an 80% tax exemption on qualifying profits from IP (e.g., software code). This results in an effective corporate tax rate of just 2.5% for R&D-heavy software firms.

items.title: Talent Scarcity in Specialized Roles
items.text: While the general dev pool is growing, senior architects and DevOps engineers are in high demand. Strategic partnerships with local universities and HR agencies are crucial.

items.title: Security-by-Design
items.text: With Cyprus being a target for regional cyberactivity, enterprise software must implement robust encryption and multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a standard feature.

faqs.question: Does my software qualify for the Cyprus IP Box?
faqs.answer: Most custom software developments, mobile apps, and SaaS platforms that involve original R&D qualify, provided the intellectual property is owned by a Cyprus company.

faqs.question: Can I use external cloud providers like AWS in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Yes, AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud are fully available and widely used by Cyprus tech firms. Some banks may require data to be stored on EU servers for regulatory reasons.

faqs.question: Is English the standard language for software documentation?
faqs.answer: Yes, English is the primary language for the tech industry in Cyprus. All documentation, code comments, and project management are typically conducted in English.

heroData.title: Digital Marketing and Branding in Cyprus
heroData.subtitle: Elevate your brand in a multilingual Mediterranean hub
heroData.description: Cyprus offers a vibrant ecosystem for digital marketing, specifically tailored for the iGaming, FinTech, and Real Estate sectors. Our partner agencies provide data-driven strategies that bridge the gap between local market nuances and global brand aspirations.
heroData.bestFor: International brands entering the Cyprus market or local tech firms seeking global scale via performance marketing.

steps.title: Brand Audit & Market Positioning
steps.description: Analyzing current brand health and competitor landscape in Cyprus. Defining a unique value proposition (UVP) that resonates with the local and international demographics on the island.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Content Strategy
steps.description: Developing localized content in English and Greek. Focusing on high-impact platforms for Cyprus: Facebook (local), LinkedIn (B2B), and Instagram/TikTok (vibrant youth market).

steps.title: Performance Marketing & SEM
steps.description: Execution of high-precision Google Ads and Meta campaigns. Optimization for Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) to maximize ROI for the high-competition Forex and Real Estate sectors.

steps.title: Influencer & Community PR
steps.description: Leveraging local Cyprus influencers and community leaders for organic brand growth. Managing press relations with major local outlets like Cyprus Mail and Philenews.

steps.title: Analytics & Iterative Scaling
steps.description: Real-time monitoring of campaign performance. Using data insights to pivot strategies and scale high-performing ad sets across regional Mediterranean markets.

items.title: Multilingual Advantage
items.text: Marketing in Cyprus requires a dual-track approach. While Nicosia is traditionally more Greek-centric, Limassol is a melting pot where English and Russian language campaigns often outperform local language ads.

items.title: Regulated Ad Restrictions
items.text: Ads for Financial Services (Forex) and Gambling are strictly regulated by CySEC and the NBA. Agencies must ensure all creative assets include mandatory risk warnings and comply with disclosure laws.

items.title: Video Content Dominance
items.text: The Cyprus market has shifted heavily towards short-form video. Brands that utilize high-quality vertical video for Instagram Reels and TikTok see 3x higher engagement than static imagery.

faqs.question: Should I localize my website into Greek for Cyprus?
faqs.answer: For B2C services (Retail, Local Services), yes. For B2B or International Tech, English is usually sufficient as the primary language, but a Greek version adds significant local trust.

faqs.question: Which social platform is most popular in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: Facebook remains the most dominant for the general population, while Instagram is preferred by the under-35 demographic. LinkedIn is highly effective for professional recruitment and B2B sales.

faqs.question: Are there privacy bans on tracking in Cyprus?
faqs.answer: As part of the EU, Cyprus follows GDPR. Marketing agencies must implement robust cookie consent banners and ensure tracking pixels are compliant with privacy regulations.
